classes.title: A Trip to the Village — food, meals & the clock (رِحْلَةٌ إِلَى القَرْيَةِ)
classes.covered: A reading passage about Ahmad's day trip to the village — breakfast foods (eggs, dates, walnuts, a glass of milk, bread and cheese), shopping on the way (chicken, fish, salad, ghee, sugar), ordering lunch, helping a poor child, and a school lesson on healthy meals; her board sentences narrating a Friday in the first-person past tense (ـتُ); ordinals (first, second, third) and the clock (six, eight o'clock); meal words (وَجْبَة، سَلَطَة، بُقُولِيَّات); Qur'anic pairs she drew out: عِقَاب/عَذَاب، أَوَّل/آخِر، فَوْز/نَصْر، the gender exceptions دَار، دُنْيَا، أَرْض (feminine) and خَلِيفَة (masculine), and 90:14 إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ; photos of grapes (عِنَب/أَعْنَاب) and date palms (نَخْل/نَخِيل).

sentences.ar: اِسْتَيْقَظْتُ وَغَسَلْتُ وَجْهِي ثُمَّ شَرِبْتُ شَايًا وَبَدَأْتُ العَمَلَ فِي البَيْتِ صَبَاحًا.
sentences.en: I woke up and washed my face, then I drank tea and began work at home in the morning.
sentences.tr: istayqaẓtu wa-ghasaltu wajhī thumma sharibtu shāyan wa-badaʾtu l-ʿamala fī l-bayti ṣabāḥan

sentences.ar: عِنْدَ الظُّهْرِ أَكَلْتُ الغَدَاءَ ثُمَّ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى المَسْجِدِ لِصَلَاةِ الجُمُعَةِ وَبَعْدَهَا عُدْتُ إِلَى بَيْتِي.
sentences.en: At noon I ate lunch, then I went to the mosque for Friday prayer, and after it I returned to my house.
sentences.tr: ʿinda ẓ-ẓuhri akaltu l-ghadāʾa thumma dhahabtu ilā l-masjidi li-ṣalāti l-jumuʿati wa-baʿdahā ʿudtu ilā baytī

sentences.ar: وَعَمِلْتُ قَلِيلًا ثُمَّ انْتَهَيْتُ مِنَ العَمَلِ.
sentences.en: I worked a little more, then I finished work.
sentences.tr: wa-ʿamiltu qalīlan thumma ntahaytu mina l-ʿamal

sentences.en: I am always hungry.
sentences.tr: anā dāʾiman jawʿān

sentences.ar: أَكَلَ بَيْضَةً أُولَى، ثُمَّ ثَانِيَةً وَثَالِثَةً.
sentences.en: He ate a first egg, then a second and a third.
sentences.tr: akala bayḍatan ūlā, thumma thāniyatan wa-thālithah

sentences.en: I prefer helping the poor.
sentences.tr: ufaḍḍilu musāʿadata l-fuqarāʾ

sentences.ar: وَجْبَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ لَا تَكْفِي طَوَالَ اليَوْمِ.
sentences.en: One meal is not enough for the whole day.
sentences.tr: wajbatun wāḥidatun lā takfī ṭawāla l-yawm

sentences.ar: لِمَاذَا لَا نَذْهَبُ إِلَى القَرْيَةِ مَرَّةً ثَانِيَةً الأُسْبُوعَ القَادِمَ؟
sentences.en: Why don't we go to the village again next week?
sentences.tr: limādhā lā nadhhabu ilā l-qaryati marratan thāniyatan al-usbūʿa l-qādim?

sentences.ar: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَنَاوَلَ طَعَامًا صِحِّيًّا كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.

sentences.tr: urīdu an atanāwala ṭaʿāman ṣiḥḥiyyan kulla yawm

sentences.en: The food was very delicious.

grammar.why: Her board: اسْتَيْقَظْتُ وَغَسَلْتُ … شَرِبْتُ … بَدَأْتُ … أَكَلْتُ … ذَهَبْتُ … عُدْتُ … عَمِلْتُ … انْتَهَيْتُ — a whole day in the first-person past.
grammar.name: ـتُ — ‘I did it’: the past tense for yourself

grammar.why: بَيْضَةً أُولَى، ثُمَّ ثَانِيَةً وَثَالِثَةً; the clock السَّاعَةُ السَّادِسَةُ / الثَّامِنَةُ; مَرَّةً ثَانِيَةً (again).
grammar.name: first, second, third — and how the clock tells time

grammar.why: Her explicit note: دَار، دُنْيَا، أَرْض are feminine without ة; خَلِيفَة is masculine with ة.
grammar.name: masculine and feminine — the ة rule and its famous exceptions

grammar.why: The passage is told in the third-person past (اسْتَيْقَظَ، أَكَلَ، شَرِبَ، ذَهَبَ، رَأَى، اشْتَرَى، جَلَسُوا) against the present-tense routines of 27 Sep.
grammar.name: past vs present — the two verb shapes

grammar.why: ثُمَّ، وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ، وَعِنْدَمَا، فَـ، and أَمَّا أُخْتُهُ فَطَلَبَتْ for contrast.
grammar.name: the connectors — and, so, then

notes: Counting 3–10 takes the plural: ثَلَاثُ تَمَرَاتٍ، ثَلَاثُ سَاعَاتٍ.
Collective vs unit: تَمْر/تَمْرَة، جَوْز/جَوْزَة، بَيْض/بَيْضَة، عِنَب/عِنَبَة; plural of the collective: أَعْنَاب، نَخِيل.
Qur'anic pair she drew: نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنَابٍ (2:266, 17:91, 36:34) — the village photos were of exactly these.
Three words for hunger/famine in rising severity: جُوع → مَجَاعَة → مَسْغَبَة (90:14) → مَخْمَصَة (5:3, 9:120).
فَوْز (triumph, attaining) vs نَصْر (victory over an opponent); both Qur'anic: الفَوْزُ العَظِيمُ, نَصْرٌ مِنَ اللهِ.
questions: What homework did she set for Sunday 18 Oct? (contract written with the passage + past-tense retelling as default tasks)

classes.title: A Working Day & The Protection Surahs (يَوْمُ العَمَل والمعوذتان)
classes.covered: Daily work routines and days off (waking early vs late, hours of the day, chores, helping parents, eating breakfast, travel); and Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas focusing on deep protection concepts (Isti'adhah as fleeing to sanctuary, Falaq as the cleaving of darkness, Ghasiq and Waqab as penetrating nightfall, Naffathat as witchcraft blowing on knots, Hasad as destructive malice, Waswas and Khannas as repetitive slinking whispers, and the chest/sadr as the outer fortress protecting the qalb).

reading.titleEn: A Working Day & The Day Off

notes: Taught Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas as conceptual protections rather than flat 1-word English glosses.
Highlighted Isti'adhah (أَعُوذُ ... مِنْ) as total movement fleeing from vulnerability to Allah's sanctuary.
Contrast: Falaq invokes 1 attribute of Allah (Rabb) against 4 external worldly harms; Nas invokes 3 attributes (Rabb, Malik, Ilah) against 1 internal spiritual harm (waswas attacking faith).
Spiritual anatomy: Al-Waswas attacks the صدر (chest / outer perimeter) because it cannot enter the قلب (heart) without an invitation.

classes.title: The flat, the week, the family
classes.covered: A flat room by room and the furniture in it; the seven days of the week; the mother's side of the family and how to make the dual; and a reading passage about Samer looking for a flat that she gave him to practise — he has not read it yet.

grammar.why: The spine of the whole class — عِنْدِي / عِنْدَكُمْ, and both ways to negate it (مَا عِنْدِي, لَيْسَ عِنْدِي), which she gave together.
grammar.name: عِندَ — having, and not having

grammar.why: Her board question مَاذَا يُوجَدُ فِي بَيْتِكَ مِنَ الأَثَاثِ؟ — the way Arabic says 'there is'.
grammar.name: يُوجَدُ — there is, there are

grammar.why: خَالَانِ وَخَالَتَانِ — she taught the dual AND how to form it, and he asked for it to be explained properly. Arabic counts one, two, and many; the ـَانِ ending IS the two, and it becomes ـَيْنِ after a preposition.
grammar.name: the dual — how to make “exactly two”

grammar.why: غُرْفَةُ نَوْمٍ, غُرْفَةُ الجُلُوسِ — two nouns pushed together with no word for 'of'. Already on the site; this class is where it earns its keep in everyday speech.
grammar.name: idafa — possession by pairing

grammar.why: مَا and لَيْسَ, as she used them with عِنْدَ.
grammar.name: the four ways to say 'not'

notes: أَرَادَ أَنْ + present (أَرَادَ أَنْ يَبْحَثَ — 'he wanted to look for') runs through the passage.
Floors are ordinals: الدَّوْر الثَّالِث, the third floor.
Feminine agreement carries the whole description of the flat: الشَّقَّة جَمِيلَة وَوَاسِعَة.
Weather (ثَلْج، مَطَر، سَحَاب) came up as an aside off ثَلْج, not as a topic. The words are carded but do not take a lesson.
